Data from 1999-2008 and diabetic inpatient encounters only; lacks external or prospective validation.

hba1c_validation_experiment.title: HbA1c Tested Binary Feature Validation Experiment

cohort_difference.clinical_interpretation: Observational association, not causation: tested patients had a 1.75 percentage point lower 30-day readmission rate (9.94% vs. 11.68%), likely because inpatient testing reflects structured diabetic care management and discharge planning rather than testing itself preventing readmissions.

hba1c_validation_experiment.conclusion: Adding binary A1C tested yielded marginal AUC change (+0.0007 in LR, +0.0035 in CatBoost, -0.0002 in XGBoost) with minimal recall and precision impact. Deployed production model remains untouched pending clinician decision.

mentor_checklist.notes: Zero patient overlap across splits (Train=48,973, Val=6,979, Test=14,038 unique patients). All modeling & tuning on validation.
Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, ROC-AUC, Brier score reported for all 6 models at common (0.120) and tuned cutoffs.
Evaluated Recall, Precision, and Lift at top 20%, 30%, and 40% flag rates across all 6 models.
Selection rule stated up front: highest validation AUC. CatBoost (0.6714) and Ensemble (0.6707) transparently compared.
Interactive 31-cutoff sweep with 18% precision capacity floor and plain-language flag translation.
Recall-first prioritized: FN is unmonitored acute deterioration; FP is manageable care coordination time.
500 sample (seed 55) matched on flag rate, High-tier share, and readmission rate. Automated parity error < 1e-6.
Tested 9.94% vs Untested 11.68% (diff 1.75 pp [1.24%, 2.25%], chi2 = 42.56). Documented as observational association.
9 clinical categories mapped from ICD-9 diagnostic codes (1999–2008 data). Zero ICD-10 references.
Target <30 = 1. Terminal discharges (2,423) excluded. StandardScaler and OneHotEncoder fitted strictly on train split.
Per-group TPR with 95% CIs reported across race, gender, age. Mitigated claims removed; group cutoffs marked analysis only.
Odds ratios include units (per 1 SD for numeric; vs ref for categorical) and rehab/SNF observational caveat.
Zero dollar signs in text and artifacts. Formatted in standard plain ASCII and Unicode.
